title: Baseline Recording
subtitle: Know the starting state for this session
altText: Chalkboard-style clinical diagram illustrating baseline recording within a neurofeedback closed loop.
learningObjectives: Explain baseline recording without diagnostic overreach.
Distinguish measurement, mechanism and clinical outcome in baseline recording.
Identify one safety or validity limitation relevant to baseline recording.

sections.explainSimply: A short baseline shows what the signal looks like before feedback begins.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Baseline interpretation must consider eyes open or closed, posture, vigilance, medication, anxiety, sleep and recent activity.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Within-session baselines can support threshold selection and quality checks but are not substitutes for validated diagnostic assessment.
sections.thinkOfItLike: A rehabilitation plan: define the target, dose, measurement and stopping rule before changing the exercise.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Psychologists need to understand baseline recording to evaluate mechanism claims, informed consent, treatment fit and whether change transfers to real-world function.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: A single baseline is a state sample, not the person’s permanent brain signature.
sections.clinicalPearl: The trained metric is an intermediate target; the clinical endpoint is meaningful function.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician using baseline recording predefines the target, checks raw signal and artifacts, monitors symptoms and function, and reviews whether change generalises beyond the feedback display.
sections.limitationsCautions: A single baseline is a state sample, not the person’s permanent brain signature. Evidence classification: established measurement principle.
